Section One

Research Questions

What shape does emotion take as it unfolds across a medical research article?

corpus.bfsu.edu.cn
01 — Research Questions 4 / 15

Motivation & Questions

Emotion arcs have been studied in novels and films — but academic discourse has received little attention from this perspective. Most existing studies represent emotion as simply positive or negative. The VAD dimensional model offers a finer-grained representation, yet has rarely been applied to academic writing.
RQ1

Do medical research articles exhibit identifiable emotion trajectories across the three VAD dimensions (Valence, Arousal, Dominance)?

RQ2

Do these trajectories differ systematically across the four IMRaD sections — Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion?

02

Section Two

Literature Review

What do we know about emotion in academic writing, and where are the gaps?

corpus.bfsu.edu.cn
02 — Literature Review 6 / 15

What We Know — and the Gaps

1

Positivity Bias

Studies document a linguistic positivity bias across academic genres — a tendency toward positive expression that has strengthened over time.

2

Section-Level Variation

Sentiment scores vary across discourse units (sections, moves), suggesting emotion is patterned by communicative function.

3

Methodological Limit

Existing studies assign a single score to a predefined unit — they cannot capture how emotion shifts continuously over an article.

4

The VAD Model

Valence (pleasant↔unpleasant) · Arousal (activated↔calm) · Dominance (in-control↔submissive) — rarely applied to academic writing.

Research Gap: Emotion arcs have been identified in novels and films — but academic discourse has received little attention, and the VAD model remains underused in genre analysis.

03

Section Three

Research Design

Corpus, lexicon, rolling-window method, and statistical framework.

corpus.bfsu.edu.cn
03 — Research Design 8 / 15

Corpus & Method

Corpus

3,600 Medical research articles
IMRaD structure, auto-extracted via Python
13.6M Total tokens across the corpus

Statistical Tests

  • A
    RQ1: Spearman's rho — each article vs. corpus median, to assess cross-article consistency
  • B
    RQ2: Friedman test + Kendall's W (effect size) — section-level VAD differences

Rolling-Window Procedure

  • 1
    Score each word using the NRC-VAD Lexicon on V, A, D scales
  • 2
    Slide a 500-token window one token at a time; compute average VAD score at each position
  • 3
    Normalize each article's trajectory to a common scale (0–100%)
  • 4
    Map onto IMRaD structure → three continuous emotion curves per article

04

Section Four

Results

Valence and Dominance stay positive — but Arousal tells a different, highly consistent story.

corpus.bfsu.edu.cn
04 — Results 10 / 15

VAD Trajectories: Overview

Valence & Dominance V & D

  • Both remain positive throughout — consistent with documented positivity bias
  • Cross-article shape consistency is low
  • Median Spearman's ρ for Valence = 0.064
Individual articles do not share a common trajectory shape on V and D. No identifiable arc.

Arousal A ★

  • Remains negative throughout — calm, low-activation register
  • Traces a clear fall-rise arc: drops to lowest in Methods, rises to peak in Discussion
  • Median Spearman's ρ = 0.758 — strong cross-article consistency
This arc is reliably reproduced across individual articles, and its turning points align closely with IMRaD boundaries.
corpus.bfsu.edu.cn
04 — Results 11 / 15

The Arousal Arc Across IMRaD

Median Arousal Trajectory — Rolling Window Analysis

Higher curve = more activation; curve is negative throughout (calm register). Median Spearman's ρ = 0.758

📉 Falls in Methods 📈 Rises through Results 🔝 Peaks in Discussion ↘ Slight dip at close
corpus.bfsu.edu.cn
04 — Results 12 / 15

Section-Level Differences (Friedman Tests)

Kendall's W — Effect Size by Dimension

ArousalW = 0.827 ★★★
DominanceW = 0.159
ValenceW = 0.003 (negligible)

Arousal shows by far the strongest differentiation across IMRaD sections. Valence carries almost no practical significance despite statistical significance.

Arousal — Section Ranking (High → Low)

  1. 1

    Discussion — highest arousal; auxiliaries & modals drive activation

  2. 2

    Introduction — moderate; framing language

  3. 3

    Results — lower; empirical description

  4. 4

    Methods — lowest; procedural, calm register

All 6 pairwise section comparisons are statistically significant. Top negative contributors in Methods/Results = content vocabulary; in Introduction/Discussion = function words (modals, auxiliaries).

05

Section Five

Implications

What these findings mean for theory, methodology, and language teaching.

corpus.bfsu.edu.cn
05 — Implications 14 / 15

Three Layers of Significance

🔬

Theoretical

  • VAD dimensions capture distinct aspects of affect — they are not interchangeable
  • Arousal is sensitive to genre-internal functional variation in ways polarity analysis cannot detect
  • Dimensional models offer a richer lens for academic discourse analysis
⚙️

Methodological

  • Rolling-window + time normalization + IMRaD mapping = a replicable framework
  • Applicable across disciplines, genres, and historical periods
  • Adapts the emotion-arc approach from fiction to academic discourse
📚

Pedagogical

  • Different IMRaD sections carry different affective expectations
  • Students can be guided to manage emotional resources deliberately across sections
  • High-contribution emotion words → basis for an ESP-oriented pedagogical lexicon
